Prototype walkthrough · film 1 of 1

An engine that refuses is not an engine that is slow

Every path that reported a failed search ended with the same sentence — that is usually temporary, try again — which is true of a timeout and false of the most likely first experience of a configured engine: SearXNG answers 403 to every query until an instance opts into JSON, so a first run refuses everything, permanently, and the report recommended waiting. Three faults now, split on whether the engine answered at all, which is HTTP's rule rather than a guess about one provider. A reader is told only whether asking again is worth anything; the variable, the file and the status code go to whoever is holding the terminal. Running it against a refusing server found the surface no test reached: the whole-run refusal, which renders from a kind rather than a sentence.

The full source is in the pull request. github.com/larry94555/competitive-landscape

All the films

  • 1. An engine that refuses is not an engine that is slownow playing
The recording has no audio. Subtitles are on by default, so it reads fine muted. Narration is optional and spoken by your browser — and it sets the pace: the video pauses while each line is read, then continues, so nothing is cut off mid-sentence.

To pause: press space, click the picture, or use the button in the bar. Any of the three stops the narration too — otherwise the voice would keep talking over a still frame.

This is a prototype, not the product. Invented companies on the reserved .example domain, no working system behind it, throwaway code. It exists to answer one question before any production code is written: does a 90–180 second wait read as work happening, or as a hang?
